title: WWF/ZSL Living Planet Report 2026: Monitored Wildlife Down 73% Since 1970, but Tigers and Green Turtles Rebound
detail: WWF and the Zoological Society of London released the Living Planet Report 2026, titled 'The Science of Hope', on October 8, 2026. It finds monitored wildlife populations fell an average of 73% between 1970 and 2022, but highlights recoveries: wild tiger numbers rose from about 3,200 (2010) to about 5,700 (2025), and the green sea turtle became the first marine turtle downlisted from Endangered to Least Concern on the IUCN Red List, with monitored nesting clutches up from roughly 419,000 (2011) to 526,000 (2024). Figures are as reported by secondary coverage and should be checked against the report itself.

media.caption: WWF Living Planet Report 2026 reveals a 'rational basis for hope'
